findings.title: Security vulnerability in flight booking system
findings.summary_md: A data leak at Amadeus exposed passenger data, with access credentials visible in plain text via an unprotected heap dump. Amadeus said it was made aware on September 21, 2026 of a potential vulnerability affecting a display environment for travel bookings, that certain booking data may have been accessible while payment or financial data could not be accessed, and that the vulnerability has since been fixed. heise online reported that readers alerted it to the issue and that current booking data, including full names, dates of birth, PNRs, and contact, ID, and passport data in plain text, was retrievable.

findings.title: Korean Air, Asiana Airlines Customer Data Leaked via Amadeus
findings.summary_md: Korean Air and Asiana Airlines reported that customer reservation information leaked through Amadeus IT Group, which operates their reservation and ticketing systems. Korean Air said unauthorized access occurred between August 2023 and September 2026 and that leaked data included names, dates of birth, email addresses, phone numbers and passport numbers. Asiana said payment information was not included because a separate system handles transactions.

findings.title: Amadeus Data Exposures: Korean Air, Asiana, Lufthansa and Condor
findings.summary_md: Two separate Amadeus exposures surfaced in October 2026: Korean Air and Asiana said booking data leaked through misuse of an Amadeus system account between August 2023 and September 2026, and heise online found passenger records for Lufthansa, Condor and others behind an open Spring Boot heap dump. Amadeus confirmed to heise a display-environment vulnerability it was made aware of on September 21, 2026, said payment data could not be accessed, and said it fixed the flaw and strengthened monitoring. No CVE, indicators of compromise, or affected counts had been published as of October 26, 2026.

findings.title: Japan Airlines warns of data breach as country grapples with multiple cyber incidents
findings.summary_md: Japan Airlines said Amadeus IT Group, which runs its flight reservation, ticketing and check-in systems, informed the firm last week that hackers accessed a portion of customer reservation data for Japan Airlines and Japan Transocean Air flights. In total 92,000 customers were impacted, with names, reservation codes and flight information accessed, and passport numbers, frequent flyer numbers, email addresses and phone numbers for about 2,000 customers. JAL said flight operations were unaffected and credit card numbers were not compromised.

findings.title: JAL Data Breach Affects 92,000 Customers
findings.summary_md: Japan Airlines disclosed the incident on 28 October 2026, five days after receiving notification from Amadeus on 23 October 2026. About 92,000 customers had reservation information exposed, including names, routes and some passport details, while no technical indicators of compromise had been published by JAL or Amadeus as of 28 October 2026.

findings.title: Amadeus Cyberattack: What Four Asian Airlines Reported
findings.summary_md: Japan Airlines reported 92,000 affected customers in a breach at Amadeus, while All Nippon Airways and Japan Transocean Air were also investigating unauthorized access to reservation records. JAL said flight operations were unaffected and credit card numbers were not compromised, and planned to contact affected customers individually with phishing warnings.
